framework_name: CIS Amazon Web Services Foundations Benchmark v1.4.0

controls.title: IAM users receive permissions only through groups
controls.text: Permissions should be attached to groups or roles rather than directly to individual IAM users, so access is managed in one place and is auditable per role rather than per person.

controls.title: IAM policies that allow full "*:*" administrative privileges are not attached
controls.text: IAM policies must not grant "Effect": "Allow" with "Action": "*" over "Resource": "*"; scope permissions to what a role or user actually needs.

controls.title: S3 buckets employ encryption at rest
controls.text: Every S3 bucket should have default server-side encryption enabled so objects are encrypted at rest without depending on each uploader to set it.

controls.title: S3 bucket policy allows only HTTPS requests
controls.text: S3 bucket policies should explicitly deny non-HTTPS requests so data in transit to and from the bucket is always encrypted.

controls.title: S3 buckets are configured with 'Block public access (bucket settings)'
controls.text: All four S3 Block Public Access settings (block public ACLs, block public policy, ignore public ACLs, restrict public buckets) should be enabled unless a bucket is deliberately public.

controls.title: EBS volume encryption is enabled
controls.text: EBS volumes should be encrypted at rest, ideally via account-level default EBS encryption rather than relying on each volume being created correctly.

controls.title: Encryption is enabled for RDS instances
controls.text: RDS instances and their storage should have encryption at rest enabled at creation time, since it cannot be enabled retroactively without a snapshot-and-restore.

controls.title: CloudTrail is enabled in all regions
controls.text: A multi-region CloudTrail trail should be enabled so API activity is recorded in every region, including ones the account does not intentionally use.

controls.title: CloudTrail log file validation is enabled
controls.text: CloudTrail log file validation should be enabled so delivered log files can be proven unmodified since CloudTrail wrote them.

controls.title: S3 bucket access logging is enabled
controls.text: S3 buckets should have server access logging enabled so requests against the bucket are recorded for later security investigation.

controls.title: CloudTrail logs are encrypted at rest using KMS CMKs
controls.text: CloudTrail log files should be encrypted at rest with a customer-managed KMS key, so reading the audit trail requires a key permission as well as bucket access.

controls.title: Rotation for customer created symmetric CMKs is enabled
controls.text: Customer-managed symmetric KMS keys should have automatic annual rotation enabled, so the material protecting long-lived data changes without re-encrypting it.

controls.title: VPC flow logging is enabled in all VPCs
controls.text: VPC flow logs should be enabled on every VPC so rejected and accepted traffic can be reconstructed during an investigation.

controls.title: No Network ACLs allow ingress from 0.0.0.0/0 to remote server administration ports
controls.text: Network ACLs should not permit inbound traffic from 0.0.0.0/0 to remote administration ports such as 22 (SSH) or 3389 (RDP).

controls.title: No security groups allow ingress from 0.0.0.0/0 to remote server administration ports
controls.text: Security groups should not permit inbound traffic from 0.0.0.0/0 to remote administration ports such as 22 (SSH) or 3389 (RDP); restrict to known source ranges.

controls.title: The default security group of every VPC restricts all traffic
controls.text: Each VPC's default security group should allow no inbound or outbound traffic, since anything launched without an explicit security group inherits it.
